provisional_claims.summary: Specimens dropped the plant's vitality. press_specimen left `vitality` out of the entry, but save validation requires it and WORKBENCH.md says specimens preserve plant measurements. So any `specimen` command failed in execute (ValueError: vitality must be an integer from 0 to 100), and the Markdown export (which prints item['vitality']) would crash.
provisional_claims.reproduction: python3 -m mosslight new g.json --seed 34; python3 -m mosslight command g.json '{"op":"specimen","args":{"x":0,"y":0}}' fails with a vitality validation error on a living plant. examples/lantern-hollow.json shows the expected specimen with vitality 71.

provisional_claims.summary: Care plans never advanced after a successful run. run_plans held the plan entry fetched before tend_many, but tend_many replaces world.__dict__ (including workbench) with a validated trial copy. The `remaining`/`day`/`status` updates therefore went to a detached dict, so the plan stayed pending on a past day and never ran again. Fix: look the entry up again after tend_many.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Schedule {"op":"schedule","args":{"name":"p","day":2,"tiles":[[0,0]],"action":"water","repeat":3,"runs":3}} then grow 5 days. Before the fix the plan still had day 2 and remaining 3 (it ran once and was then stuck). After the fix it has day 8 and remaining 1, as in examples/lantern-hollow.json.

provisional_claims.summary: Revision numbers drifted by more than one per command. execute() set trial.revision = trial.revision + 1, stacking on top of the function's own increments (grow 5 days added 6, most edits added 2). Each command should be one edit and advance the revision by exactly one from the source world, matching examples/lantern-hollow.json (16 replayed commands → revision 16).
provisional_claims.reproduction: Replay examples/hollow-actions.json on `new --seed 34`: revision came out 37 instead of 16. A single tend command on revision 0 produced revision 2.

provisional_claims.summary: gardening.rectangle omitted the right-hand column (range(left, right) instead of inclusive right+1), so rectangular selections/blueprints lost a column.
provisional_claims.reproduction: w=create(1,8,6); len(gardening.rectangle(w,0,0,3,2)) returned 9, expected 12 (4x3 inclusive).

provisional_claims.summary: Circular brush used the diamond (Manhattan) test, so shape="circle" was identical to diamond; now uses Euclidean dx²+dy² <= r².
provisional_claims.reproduction: brush(w,4,4,2,"circle") returned 13 tiles (same as diamond) and omitted (5,5); correct circle radius 2 includes diagonal (1,1) offsets → 21 tiles.

provisional_claims.summary: Transplant discarded the plant's stress (set destination stress to 0) although docs say a transplant carries age and stress; destination now receives source stress, source resets.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Set tile stress 40 on a plant at (0,0); transplant to (3,0); destination stress was 0, expected 40.

provisional_claims.summary: Prune could produce negative age and vitality above 100 (invalid save that fails reload). Now clamps age>=0 and vitality<=100.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Plant moss (age 0, vit 52) then prune → age -5; set vitality 98 and prune → 106; World.from_dict(to_dict()) then raises.

provisional_claims.summary: craft checked only per-unit cost (stock < cost) instead of cost*amount, allowing negative inventory balances when crafting multiples.
provisional_claims.reproduction: inventory fiber=2; craft('mulch', amount=3) succeeded leaving fiber=-4; now raises "Need 6 fiber".

provisional_claims.summary: Nursery watering added only 1 hydration instead of restoring the documented three-day supply.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Start a batch, grow 2 days (hydration 1), nursery_water → hydration 2; docs: watering restores a three-day supply (3).

provisional_claims.reproduction: Clover batch (maturity 2) with hydration 0: advance_nursery twice → became ready while dry. Expected age unchanged, vitality -20 each day.

provisional_claims.summary: plant_out only took 4 nutrients for the last seedling of a batch; every planted seedling should use four nutrient points from its site.

provisional_claims.reproduction: On day 0, schedule(w,"p",1,[[0,0]],"water") raised; it should be accepted and run during the next grow.

provisional_claims.summary: Standalone art SVGs made every tile focusable. render_svg always put tabindex="0" role="button" on each tile group, even when interactive=False, so exported artwork (CLI `render`) had keyboard-focus buttons that don't do anything. Only interactive studio maps should get those attributes, as in render_map and examples/lantern-hollow.svg (`<g class="tile" data-x="0" data-y="0" >`).
provisional_claims.reproduction: Replay examples/hollow-actions.json on seed 34 and render_svg(world). Before the fix the output differs from examples/lantern-hollow.svg at the first tile (tabindex present). After the fix it matches byte for byte.

provisional_claims.summary: Conditional rules were evaluated sequentially against a mutating garden, so an earlier rule's care changed whether later rules fired. Now all rule conditions are evaluated against the post-growth snapshot, then actions are applied.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Two rules on same tile: rule1 moisture below 30 → water; rule2 moisture below 30 → compost. Tile moisture 10 after growth: rule2 was skipped because rule1 raised moisture to 42. Expected both to fire.

provisional_claims.summary: Campaigns ran under the wrong ecological release. runtime.execution_version() always returned CURRENT_VERSION ("conservation-2"), so compute/replay ignored the release recorded in the campaign definition (e.g. `--version classic-1`). The fix returns definition["runtime"]["id"], so campaigns resume with their recorded release as CAMPAIGNS.md requires.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Create a classic-1 campaign with a rain_barrel treatment on a rainy period and work it to completion. Barrel tiles got conservation-2 delivery (capped by deficit) instead of the classic +6. CampaignStore.compute used execution_version(definition) regardless of definition["runtime"]["id"].

provisional_claims.summary: Campaigns: (1) runtime.execution_version ignored the recorded release and always executed with conservation-2, so classic-1 campaigns resumed/replayed under the wrong ecology; now uses definition["runtime"]["id"]. (2) CampaignStore.publish accepted stale workers (`generation = ? OR owner != ?`) — now requires matching generation AND owner. (3) publish committed the branch state before writing its checkpoint/report (COMMIT/BEGIN mid-transaction), breaking atomic single coherent history; now one transaction. (4) compact computed protected descendant fork origins but never used them, deleting checkpoints referenced by child lineages (breaking provenance); now kept. (5) fork re-applied events already performed at the checkpoint offset (offset <= event) — now only strictly later events carry over.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Create campaign with --version classic-1 and a rain_barrel treatment; worked results equal conservation-2 barrel behavior. Publish with stale claim (different owner, old generation) returned True and overwrote state. Fork at offset 3 from a branch with event at offset 3 → continuation's offset-0 event re-applied (double watering). compact(parent, 5) after fork at offset 3 deleted checkpoint (1,3) and provenance(child) raised "Checkpoint is unavailable".

provisional_claims.summary: Stale or foreign campaign workers could publish. CampaignStore.publish used `(generation = ? OR owner != ?)`, so a worker whose lease had expired and been reclaimed (newer generation/owner) could still overwrite branch state with its outdated result. This forks the progress history. Fix: require `generation = ? AND owner = ?`, the same as fail().
provisional_claims.reproduction: Worker A claims a branch with a 1 s lease. The clock advances, worker B reclaims (generation+1) and publishes. A then publishes its old state: before the fix A's publish returned True and overwrote the state and next_offset. After the fix it is rejected.

provisional_claims.summary: Campaign publish was not atomic. It committed the branch-state update, then opened a second transaction for the checkpoint row and final report archive. A crash or error between the two left a branch that had advanced (possibly complete) with no checkpoint or report, breaking "a single coherent history" and leaving forks unable to find checkpoints. Fix: state update, checkpoint and report archive now happen in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Make _checkpoint raise (e.g. by pre-inserting a checkpoint row for the next offset). Before the fix the branch state was already committed as advanced with no checkpoint. After the fix the whole publish rolls back.

provisional_claims.summary: Engine ecology defects: season offset (day 0 must be Dawn), neighbor moisture read from partially-updated cells instead of the day's snapshot, bare ground not recovering 1 nutrient/day, comfort using base shade instead of effective (shade cloth) shade, Hush penalizing glowcaps, fixed 105-day lifespan instead of species lifespan (glowcap 75), strain nutrient return keyed off the previous day's vitality instead of the day's result.
provisional_claims.reproduction: create(34,16,11); step(w,24) now reproduces examples/first-garden.json cells and journal exactly (before: season journal wrong and 2+ cells off). season(0) == 'Dawn'. A glowcap aged 76 now dies; shade cloth changes comfort.

provisional_claims.summary: Compaction deleted checkpoints that forks were created from. compact() computed the `protected` set of (ordinal, offset) lineage anchors but never used it, so a checkpoint off the keep interval was removed even though a descendant was forked from it. provenance() on the child then failed with "Checkpoint is unavailable", contradicting "keeping ... the origins of existing descendants".
provisional_claims.reproduction: Create an 8-day campaign, work it to completion, fork branch 2 at offset 4, then compact the parent with --every 5. Before the fix provenance(child) raised; after the fix the checkpoint at (2,4) survives.

provisional_claims.summary: Campaign forks repeated care that had already happened. fork() copied parent events with `offset <= event.offset`, which includes events at the checkpoint offset itself, even though the checkpoint state already contains them. The continuation then applied them again at its offset 0. CAMPAIGNS.md: "care already performed at the checkpoint remains part of its starting garden". Fix: copy only events with offset strictly after the checkpoint.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Use the examples/treatments.json campaign ("Extra water" waters at offsets 1 and 4) and fork branch 2 at offset 4. Before the fix the continuation had event offset 0 → water again (double watering). After the fix it has no events.

provisional_claims.summary: Habitat/weather/analysis/gardening/nursery/notebook/planning fixes: shade cloth missing the tile below; rain barrels adding water on dry days; stress rising at vitality exactly 30; worms ignoring peat; almanac dry spell counted drizzle days; season_day offset; calendar showing one plan occurrence too many; nursery watering only +1 instead of restoring 3 days; dry nursery days still developing; plant_out only using nutrients for the last seedling; note search end date exclusive & tag substring match; specimens dropping vitality (breaks save validation); complete_task ignoring done=false; overdue including today; task lists not sorted by due date; bed names duplicate check case-sensitive; plans rejecting tomorrow.
provisional_claims.reproduction: e.g. press_specimen then World.from_dict(world.to_dict()) raised 'vitality must be an integer'; complete_task(w,id,False) left done=True; schedule(w,...,day=w.day+1) rejected; water_batch with hydration 0 gave 1; add_bed 'Moss' then 'moss' allowed but save invalid.

provisional_claims.summary: History replay checkpoint key hashed only the last event (events[-1:]), so a corrected history reused cached state from the uncorrected history whenever later events shared IDs, returning stale gardens. Key now covers the full event prefix.
provisional_claims.reproduction: create; append note A (e1); append note B (e2); correct {e1: null} → replay of [e2] hit checkpoint keyed by e2 from original history, so the corrected garden still contained note A. verify() with use_cache=False mismatched.

provisional_claims.summary: Commands/experiments/exchange/charts/server/CLI/model/state fixes: execute accepted extra keys and missing op; experiment re-applied every event at every later offset, allowed case-variant duplicate names, dropped final sample, and reported deltas as control-minus-treatment; import_csv bumped revision twice; blueprint mirror/rotation off by one; shade map ignored structures; history chart x-axis used indexes not dates; server publish replaced world before a failed save, kept oldest 30 undo entries, never cleared redo on new edits, accepted stale-but-greater/boolean revisions, legacy import (no revision) overwrote revision, undo reused old revision numbers; CLI exited 1 instead of 2 and forecast same-path check was string-based; empty cells with only age or vitality accepted; ids equal to next_id accepted; plants on stone accepted; duplicate history days accepted.
provisional_claims.reproduction: replay(create(34,16,11), examples/hollow-actions.json) now matches examples/lantern-hollow.json including revision 16. transform_blueprint(mirror=True) previously produced x == width (invalid). experiment with offset-1 water event previously watered every day.

provisional_claims.summary: History reference resolution used the authoring-time numeric binding instead of the logical reference's current local ID, so after a correction renumbered objects, later edits targeted the wrong (or missing) object. _resolved_command now uses entity["id"].
provisional_claims.reproduction: append note A (id1), note B (id2), edit_note ident 2; correct removing note A → note B becomes id1 but edit event still sent ident 2 → conflict/missing. Now edit applies to B.

provisional_claims.summary: Cherry-pick identified events by command content digest, so independently authored identical actions (e.g. two separate "water 0,0" events) were merged/dropped. Identity now uses the authored event ID: shared actions included once, independent actions stay distinct.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Target and source each independently append the same command {"op":"tend","args":{"x":0,"y":0,"action":"water"}}; cherry_pick source event into target → it was skipped as "already present". Now appended.

provisional_claims.summary: Rebase ordering only respected the target branch's order of shared events, so contradictory local orderings were silently resolved in favor of target. _respect_shared_order now enforces both local and target orders and raises order-conflict when they contradict.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Fork where child and parent end up with shared events in opposite orders (e.g. via picks); rebase silently used target order instead of reporting "order-conflict".

provisional_claims.summary: Staged studies: (1) later stages started every trial (including treatments) from the previous stage's *control* checkpoint, discarding the promoted treatments' earlier care; now each continues from its own checkpoint. (2) _advance_if_ready finalized a stage decision as soon as any source had complete results (before all trials were terminal) and never recorded a failed decision when no garden was eligible (study hung). Now waits until all jobs are complete/failed, then promotes or records the failure. Ensembles: summarize() zipped controls.values() against paired treatment rows, pairing controls with the wrong replicate when a control/treatment was missing; now pairs by replicate.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Create study with examples/study.json and work; stage-1 treatment state world equals control's stage-0 world (treatment care lost). With one failing treatment trial on one source, stage decision was saved while other jobs still pending (completion order dependent). For ensembles, if replicate A's control failed but B's succeeded, B's treatment was compared with the wrong control.

provisional_claims.summary: Rebase used the parent's current head as the merge base instead of the fork's recorded base_revision, so parent edits made after forking looked like shared base and were treated as local deletions/conflicts. Now uses source["base_revision"].
provisional_claims.reproduction: create main; fork child; append note on main; append task on child; rebase child onto main → main's new note was in "base" so the child (lacking it) removed it. Now result has note + task.

provisional_claims.summary: History correction canonicalized replacement commands against the final garden of the uncorrected branch; numeric IDs in a replacement must refer to the garden at that point in the history. Now resolves against the replayed prefix preceding the corrected event.
provisional_claims.reproduction: append note(id1); append edit_note(1); append note(id2) ... correct the edit event with edit_note ident 2 → accepted against final garden even though note 2 did not exist at that point; should conflict/resolve relative to prefix.

provisional_claims.summary: Ensembles: (1) evaluate() took the result identity from the cache origin on a cache hit, so two sources with equal saves (or treatments sharing a plan) were reported under the wrong replicate/treatment label; identity is now always the requested one. (2) report() replaced the archived envelope's result with a summary of the *current* outcomes, so published reports for earlier revisions changed after later edits/work; now returns the immutable archived envelope. (3) publish() validated only the node's previous (known) reads rather than the reads actually used by the computation, so a result computed from superseded inputs (e.g. first computation, or route switching plans) could be accepted after a concurrent edit; now checks computed reads against current inputs.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Create ensemble with two sources containing identical saves: second source's control reported identity replicate = first label (duplicate) and summarize loses a member. Work to completion, report(rev0); edit a plan, work again; report(id, 0) result now reflects revision-1 outcomes. prepare() a fresh node, edit its plan, then publish the old computation → accepted with stale inputs.

provisional_claims.summary: Courier projections could erase observations they didn't include. project() kept the per-record coverage contexts for every record, including ones it filtered out. When a projection of a checkpointed packet was merged into a complete notebook, _covered() treated those unselected records' newer events as already seen and superseded, and dropped them. COURIER.md says merging a selection preserves the observations it did not include. Fix: project() keeps contexts only for the requested records.
provisional_claims.reproduction: a puts records r and s; full = checkpoint(a); put(full, 's', {'text':'other edited'}) ... sel = project(checkpoint(a_later), ['r']); merge(full, sel). Before the fix, s's newer edit could be dropped whenever the projection's context for s covered its dot. After the fix observations include s with 'other edited'.

provisional_claims.summary: Courier merge kept a stale writer counter. merge() copied left["counter"] even when the joined clock showed the left writer at a higher counter (e.g. merging an older copy of a writer's packet with its newer copy). Continuing that writer's work after the merge ("A merged packet keeps the left writer and can be used to continue that writer's work") reissued an existing dot [peer, counter], silently overwriting an earlier event or triggering a "writer sequence reused" rejection on the next exchange. Fix: counter = max(left counter, joined clock[left peer]).
provisional_claims.reproduction: a = new_packet('A'); put(a,'r',{'text':'x'}); old = deepcopy(a); put(a,'t',{'text':'new'}); m = merge(old, a); put(m,'u',{'text':'c'}). Before the fix m['counter'] restarted from old's counter and the new events overwrote dots ["A",3]/["A",4] from record t. After the fix all 8 events are retained.

provisional_claims.summary: save_merge mapped every record to logical id ["base", id] regardless of origin, so records created independently on both replicas with the same local number were merged into one (or conflicted). New records now get [origin, id] logical ids and fresh allocation; inherited ids keep base identity.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Base with note 1; left adds note "left" (id 2), right adds note "right" (id 2); reconcile(..., left_origin="desk", right_origin="field") produced a conflict at /records/notes/["base",2]; now ready with both notes as ids 3 and 4, receipt allocation records the mapping.

provisional_claims.summary: Field courier CRDT defects: (1) precedes() iterated over b's peers, so any event whose writer was absent from another event's context was treated as superseded (concurrent edits silently lost). (2) merge only compared the record when a writer dot appeared in both packets, so conflicting reuse of an event identity was not rejected. (3) _covered used the maximum of all records' contexts, so sharing one observation made the recipient drop other records' events; now per-record. (4) observations() casefolded values when de-duplicating concurrent values (case-differing text collapsed). (5) a concurrent edit + deletion hid the observation (any False head) — now remains visible unless all alive heads are deletions. (6) acknowledged() used max instead of min across peers (reported progress not seen by every device). (7) event values aliased caller-owned objects. (8) new events used the global clock as context, so after merging a projection a later edit claimed to have seen unrelated records' edits/deletions; context is now the record's clock. (9) merged packet counter could lag the writer's known clock, causing dot reuse when continuing a writer's work.
provisional_claims.reproduction: A=new_packet('A'); put(A,'x',{'text':'X1'}); B=merge(new_packet('B'),A); remove(A,'x'); put(B,'x',{'text':'X-B'}); observations(merge(A,B)) previously hid x. put(A,'n',{'text':'Fern'}) vs put(B,'n',{'text':'fern'}) concurrently → only one value shown. acknowledged({'A':{'A':3},'B':{'A':1}},['A','B']) returned {'A':3} instead of 1. Project(A,['x']) merged into B then B edits y → A's concurrent y edit was superseded without being seen.

provisional_claims.summary: History exchange reconciliation could lose reversions after criss-cross merges. _common_bases returned only maximal[:1], the lexicographically first of several maximal common ancestors. After both collaborators had combined the same work, reconciliation used an arbitrary single base instead of the virtual merge of all bases (which comparison() is built to compute). A later reversion (e.g. correcting a note back to its original text) then looked "unchanged" against the wrong base, and the other side's stale value won. HISTORY_EXCHANGE.md: "Repeated rounds ... must retain later edits and reversions, including when both collaborators previously combined the same work." Fix: return all maximal common ancestors.
provisional_claims.reproduction: P0 has note "orig". A corrects it to "A" (P1a); B appends a task (P1b). A and B each reconcile P1a+P1b (M1, M2). A corrects the note back to "orig" (P2a on M1); B adds task t2 (P2b on M2). reconcile(P2a, P2b): with one base, whenever P1b sorts first the result keeps "A" (reversion lost). After the fix both orders give note "orig" and tasks [t, t2].

provisional_claims.summary: World.to_dict() shared journal entries with the live garden. It returned list(self.journal), a shallow copy, so the journal entry dicts were shared. Editing a returned save (e.g. d["journal"][0]["text"] = ...) silently rewrote the live garden's journal, contradicting PORTABILITY.md ("to_dict returns an independently editable save representation"). Fix: copy each entry.
provisional_claims.reproduction: w = create(1); d = w.to_dict(); d['journal'][0]['text'] = 'x'; before the fix w.journal[0]['text'] == 'x'. After the fix it is unchanged.

provisional_claims.summary: Save validation accepted the same identifier in two collections. state.validate reset its `ids` set for each collection, so a save could hold e.g. note 3 and task 3. IDs are allocated from the single shared next_id and must be unique across entities: save_merge maps id→collection and "retaining the meaning of an existing identifier" is an identity rule. Such saves were accepted and later mis-handled. Fix: check uniqueness across all collections, as the pre-loop `ids = set()` intended.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Take any v2 save with a note {id:1}, add a task with id 1 (next_id 2), and World.from_dict(save). Before the fix it loads; after the fix it raises "Identifiers must be unique and below next_id". All shipped examples still load.

provisional_claims.summary: Loading a save aliased the caller's data: workbench validation used a shallow raw.copy() (and journal entries were shared), so editing the source dict after World.from_dict mutated the loaded garden (tiles, notes, plans...). Validation now deep-copies the workbench and journal entries are copied.
provisional_claims.reproduction: d=w.to_dict(); x=World.from_dict(d); d['workbench']['tiles'][0]['mulch']=50 → x.workbench['tiles'][0]['mulch'] became 50. Now unchanged.

provisional_claims.summary: SVG artwork (render_svg / art layer) omitted the garden's authored title entirely, although docs state SVG artwork preserves authored titles as text. The illustration now includes an escaped <title> with the garden title.
provisional_claims.reproduction: rename_garden(w,"Fern hollow"); "Fern hollow" not in render_svg(w). Now present (escaped as text, e.g. "<b>" → "<b>").

provisional_claims.summary: Irrigation: max-flow allocation skipped residual (reverse) arcs so deliveries could be below the achievable maximum; schedule search merged distinct states whose aggregate census happened to match (identity must be the full world + tank + offset), losing optimal schedules.
provisional_claims.reproduction: allocate([s->a 1, a->b 1, s->b 1, a->x 1, b->y 1], 's', {'x':1,'y':1}, 5) delivered 1 before (needs reverse arc through a->b); now 2. solve() previously discarded states with equal census but different cells.

provisional_claims.summary: Field calibration regression used raw (uncentered) timestamp sums — catastrophic cancellation for epoch-scale timestamps — and did not average readings sharing a timestamp; workspace catalog format-1 upgrade REINDEXed with the old normalizer before installing the new one, so upgraded catalogs could not find NFKC/space-normalized labels.
provisional_claims.reproduction: estimate on readings at 1.7e9+{0,60,120} with moisture 42,44,43 now equals the t={0,60,120} result (43.5). Upgrading a format-1 catalog then search('Ｆｉｅｌｄ  pond') now matches 'Field pond'.

provisional_claims.summary: History exchange reconcile depended on argument order: reconcile(a,b) and reconcile(b,a) produced differently ordered event lists, so when both collaborators combined the same work (criss-cross), the next round failed with 'order-conflict'. Reconcile now canonicalizes the pair (matching comparison()'s sorted base order).
provisional_claims.reproduction: desk & field each publish from genesis, both reconcile (in opposite argument order), each adds one more edit and publishes; reconcile of the two new heads previously raised HistoryConflict order-conflict, now merges retaining the reversion and the task completion.

provisional_claims.summary: Harvest did not start a new growth period. harvest() only lowered age by 5, so any plant well past its harvest age could be harvested again immediately (and repeatedly) for full yield. WORKBENCH.md: harvesting "starts a new growth period before the next harvest". Fix: reset the plant's age to 0 on harvest (matching collect_seed's regrowth rule), so it must reach the species harvest_age again.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Set tile (0,0) to moss age 40, vitality 90; execute harvest twice. Before the fix both succeed (age 40→35→30). After the fix the first yields {'fiber': 3} and the second fails with "Harvest needs age 8 and vitality 40".

provisional_claims.summary: Ready nursery batches gained no vigor on hydrated days (vitality bonus only applied while "growing"), contradicting "Hydrated days develop the batch and improve its vigor" and the rule that batches still need watering after they are ready. Hydrated days now add vigor for all living batches.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Clover batch becomes ready (age 2); water it and grow 1 day → vitality unchanged. Expected +3 (capped at 100).

provisional_claims.summary: Garden coordinates accepted booleans. World.index used isinstance(x, int), so JSON true/false passed as coordinates 1/0 in every command (tend, terrain, transplant, notes with tiles, beds, plans...). The strict validators elsewhere (validation.integer, save loading) use type(v) is int and reject booleans. Fix: World.index requires real integers, so {"x":true} is rejected with "Coordinates must be integers".
provisional_claims.reproduction: execute(create(34), {"op":"tend","args":{"x":true,"y":false,"action":"water"}}) succeeded before the fix and watered tile (1,0) ("A slow pour reaches tile 2, 1."). After the fix it raises ValueError.

provisional_claims.summary: Art SVG regression: render_svg emitted an extra <title> element, so rendering the shipped example saves no longer reproduced the portable artwork (examples/first-garden.svg, examples/lantern-hollow.svg generated by the reference renderer). Removed the extra element; render_svg(load(examples/X.json)) now matches examples/X.svg byte-for-byte again (non-interactive art also has no tabindex/role attrs).
provisional_claims.reproduction: python3 -c "from mosslight.model import load; from mosslight.render import render_svg; print(render_svg(load('examples/lantern-hollow.json')).strip()==open('examples/lantern-hollow.svg').read().strip())" → False before, True after. Also verified replaying examples/hollow-actions.json on create(34) reproduces examples/lantern-hollow.json exactly, and create(34,16,11)+24 days reproduces examples/first-garden.json cells/journal.

provisional_claims.summary: apply_blueprint indexed tile["species"] directly although validate_blueprint accepts tiles that omit "species" (treated as no plant). Such a validated blueprint crashed with KeyError (escaping execute's ValueError contract / CLI error handling). Placement now treats a missing species as bare ground.
provisional_claims.reproduction: execute(w, {"op":"blueprint","args":{"data":{"format":"mosslight-blueprint","version":1,"width":1,"height":1,"tiles":[{"x":0,"y":0,"terrain":"sand","structure":"log"}]},"x":1,"y":1,"overwrite":true}}) raised KeyError: 'species'; now applies sand+log and clears the tile.

provisional_claims.summary: Core calendar/weather/ecology fixes: season() was shifted by one (day 0 reported Highsummer) and weather wetness used the same shifted index; phase used a 47-day year; calendar_day season_day off by one; almanac longest_dry_spell counted drizzle days instead of rainless days; next_weather searched from today instead of the future; calendar listed one extra plan occurrence (gap//repeat <= remaining). Engine: neighbor moisture mean read partially-updated cells instead of the start-of-day snapshot; plant comfort used base shade instead of effective (shade-cloth) shade; lifespan was hard-coded 105 instead of per-species (glowcap 75).
provisional_claims.reproduction: season(0) returned 'Highsummer'; calendar_day(0)['season_day']==2; almanac with drizzle-only days reported them as dry spell; schedule(day 5, repeat 3, runs 4) → calendar showed day 17 too. Replaying examples/hollow-actions.json on create(34) now reproduces examples/lantern-hollow.json exactly and create(34,16,11)+24 days reproduces examples/first-garden.json.

provisional_claims.summary: Habitat/analysis/gardening/nursery/experiment fixes: shade cloth didn't shelter the tile below (missing (x, y+1)); stress rose at vitality exactly 30 (doc: below 30); worms ignored peat. census vitality averaged over all tiles instead of living plants; diversity used log2 instead of natural log; suitability ignored structure shade; recommendations ignored empty_only=False; forecast dropped the final day when days wasn't a multiple of every. rectangle() excluded the right column; circle brush was a diamond; craft checked a single batch cost instead of cost*amount; prune could make age negative / vitality >100; transplant zeroed stress instead of carrying it. Nursery watering added 1 instead of restoring 3-day supply, dry days still aged batches, plant_out only used nutrients for the last seedling. Experiments: case-sensitive reserved/duplicate names, events re-executed on every later offset, final sample omitted, against_control deltas computed backwards (control minus treatment). Save validation allowed the same identifier in different collections.
provisional_claims.reproduction: rectangle(w,0,0,2,1) returned 4 tiles (expected 6); craft('compost', amount=3) with 3 fiber succeeded and went negative; experiment with event offset 1 and days 4 watered 4 times; forecast(days=10, every=3) ended at elapsed day 9; census diversity for two equal species = 1.0 (log2) instead of ln 2 ≈ 0.6931.
